subject: Renewal evaluation: side-by-side perf validation and contingency roadmap
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@hightide.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal evaluation and bake-off timeline

Tessa —

Thanks for the quick reply last week. As we discussed in the QBR, HighTide is starting a side-by-side evaluation ahead of our contract renewal in November. We have a formal bake-off running between Redwood and NimbusAI (their managed endpoint). Primary asks from our engineering team: throughput at 8k concurrent requests (typical 256 token avg), 99th percentile latency under 450ms for 512-token contexts, and a cost-per-1M-token comparison at our expected mix.

Can you share how Redwood would run the benchmark (config, dataset, and expected observability access)? We also need any temporary capacity uplift or trial hardware options you can provide — the vendor can propose ephemeral dedicated pools during the test window.

We care a lot about caching behavior (prefix/KV caching), cold-starts, and how you handle long-latency tail events. Also procurement wants to understand the commit terms you'd expect if we choose Dedicated for production.

--
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Engineering
HighTide

P.S. cc: eng-eval@hightide.com (they'll be the test runners)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@hightide.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal evaluation and bake-off timeline

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. We're happy to support a reproducible side-by-side. Attached is a short bench kit (Redwood_benchmark_instructions_v1.pdf) that includes:
- exact request shapes and a recommended seed dataset
- config for dedicated trial pools (GPU type, replicas, sample autoscale policy)
- how we'll surface token-level cost + p99 latency in the Console during the run

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
1) We provide a 4-week dedicated trial environment with a mirrored capacity profile.
2) HighTide runs two pre-specified test passes (synthetic load + production replay).
3) We grant read-only Console access to eng-eval and a short-lived metrics export (S3).
4) Both sides sign a one-week NDA addendum for kernel-level probes if needed.

Can you confirm the test dataset link and whether eng-eval needs SSH access to the runner for in-situ tooling? If you prefer, we can run the tests for you and share raw traces.

I booked a 30-minute sync if you want to walk through the plan live: https://meetings.redwood.ai/meet/9f4e-tessa-30m (Wed 9/15 or Thu 9/16 work for us).

Ben and Monica — tagging for capacity and trial config. If we offer a short dedicated uplift, we should predefine the KPIs that trigger credits or an escape roadmap.

Thanks,
Tessa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena@hightide.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-eval@hightide.com
Date: 2027-09-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal evaluation and bake-off timeline

Tessa — thanks. eng-eval attached the curated test set here: https://hightide-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com/hightide-test-set.tar.gz (attachment: hightide-test-set.tar.gz). The set contains 10k representative prompts and a 72-hour production replay window.

A few specifics from the bench team:
- We'll run a 48-hour peak simulation (burst profile) followed by a 24-hour steady-state.
- Please document cold-start conditions and whether KV/prefix caching is enabled by default.
- If you provide the ability to toggle quantization/optimizations, note the exact flags so we can compare apples-to-apples.

We prefer Redwood to run the first pass and share raw traces so we can avoid instrumentation drift. Wednesday 9/15 at 10:00 PT works for a quick kickoff.

Elena

On Fri, Sep 12, 2027 at 11:08 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Appreciate the clarity. We're happy to support a reproducible side-by-side...
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-13T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: HighTide trial proposal and risk notes

Tessa / Monica —

Reading Elena's note. My suggested operational play:
- Offer a 4-week Dedicated trial with a single uplift event (x2 baseline capacity for 72 hours) to show headroom.
- Include a one-time 20% trial credit if HighTide signs a 12-month reserved commit within 30 days post-trial.
- Provide the bench kit as an executable pipeline (we'll run it and drop a metrics export).

Risks: NimbusAI is offering bespoke kernel tuning and a private quantization profile — engineering flagged that the competitors sometimes tune for the customer's recall distribution which can skew cost/latency. We should log that as a comparator footnote.

Attachments: trial-config.yaml (configuration for the temporary Dedicated pool)

If we go this route, we need:
- product to pre-approve the DPU type and autoscale policy (Monica)
- legal to sign the short NDA addendum before kernel probes (Tessa)
- ops to enable read-only Console access and a timebound S3 export (Ben)

Ben
VP, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@hightide.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, eng-eval@hightide.com
Date: 2027-09-14T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal evaluation and bake-off timeline

Elena —

Thanks for the test set link. We will:
- Stand up a mirrored Dedicated trial environment (trial-config.yaml attached by Ben) for the first pass.
- Run the Redwood-executed benchmark and push raw traces to an S3 export.
- Enable read-only Console and a short-lived tracing endpoint for eng-eval.

I've attached a mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) that outlines milestones, responsible owners, and an acceptance matrix. Key call-outs:
- Acceptance KPIs: p99 latency (512 tokens) < 450ms; throughput target met at 8k concurrent profiles; cost delta <= 10% of Nimbus baseline.
- If p99 fails by >20% or cost is >25% higher, we'll provide an escape roadmap: temporary throughput credits, a prioritized tuning sprint, and a scoped SLA credit if we miss the agreed remediation timeline.

Quick Q: what procurement window do you need for an expedited commit? We'll map the credit terms to your timeline.

Looking forward to the kickoff on Wed 9/15 10:00 PT.

—Tessa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena@hightide.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-eval@hightide.com
Date: 2027-09-18T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal evaluation and bake-off timeline

Tessa —

Confirming we will proceed with Redwood running the first-pass benchmarks this week. Procurement asked for a short timeline doc for the internal buying committee (attached: procurement-timeline.pdf). A few procurement asks:
- How long is the trial window (we expected 4 weeks) and can you confirm the terms for the 20% sign-before credits?
- If the p99 SLA trigger fires and remediation takes longer than the sprint window, can credits be applied retroactively to the trial traffic?

If you can add those clarifications to the mutual_action_plan.xlsx after the kickoff, we can circulate and get legal involved. Thanks for being flexible — eng-eval will join the kickoff, and we'll share any profiler outputs they request.

Elena
Head of Platform Engineering, HighTide
